newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar regains ground to end firmer.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar regains ground to end firmer.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar regained ground from its overnight low to drift higher by the close in largely illiquid and quiet Wednesday trade.
The Kiwi closed at US$0.7053/60 from 0.7051/58 early in the session, compared to an overnight low of 0.7030.
The Trade-Weighted Index remained at nine-year highs at 68.60 from 68.55 this morning.

"There is nothing large out there at the moment and it's not moving on the back of the Aussie," said one Auckland dealer. The topside for Kiwi was seen as limited by the high TWI, which was creating a great deal of hesitance.
Exporters were playing a waiting game because they doubted the sustaintability of the TWI's gains.
Similarly a Kiwi/mark at 1.15 and Kiwi/yen at 83.5 was cited as another reason for holding back.
Overall, trade was dominated by interbank business, as had been the case since the start of the year.
